title: structured output: constrained decoding backends - CFG/regex/tokenizer edgecases
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Constrained decoding supports multiple backends (CFG/grammar, regex, and tokenizer-based constraints). We observed incorrect acceptance/rejection behavior for corner cases where tokenization boundaries and Unicode grapheme clusters interacted with regex/CFG constraints, causing structured-output parsing to silently fail or produce invalid JSON. This PR consolidates backend behavior, adds normalization/round-tripping checks for tokenizer boundaries, and hardens the CFG and regex evaluators to be robust to multi-token and multi-codepoint constraints.

Summary of changes: consolidated constraint evaluation into a common 'matcher' abstraction; implemented tokenizer-aware regex fallback for patterns that span token boundaries; improved CFG emitter to prefer valid token-aligned productions when possible; added explicit Unicode normalization step (NFKC) for constraints and input when configured; expanded test harness and new fuzz tests for tokenizer edgecases.

Impact: This fixes a class of failures reported by internal e2e tests and customer examples where short tokens split punctuation/emoji sequences. There are no expected breaking changes to public APIs; behavior for malformed user-provided grammars/regexes is more deterministic (we now return structured error metadata rather than best-effort partial matches).

Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-4215) - [x] unit tests added for tokenizer edgecases - [x] integration tests with streaming enabled - [x] benchmark sanity checked for latency regression (<3% p95 delta) - [x] docs snippet updated in redwood-docs
commits: feat(constrained): introduce matcher abstraction and tokenizer-aware regex fallback
fix(tokenizer): normalize unicode before constraint evaluation
test(constrained): add fuzz tests for multi-token regex/CFG boundaries
perf: micro-optimizations in CFG emitter to avoid extra allocations
docs: update structured-output guide with tokenizer notes
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: The tokenizer-aware regex fallback looks good, but can we avoid copying the token buffer when we compute cross-token spans? Suggest using slices where possible.
Maya Patel: Addressed in commit 3. Reworked the fallback to use borrowed slices; added benchmark to ensure no regression.

Riley Chen: Can you add a short note about normalization config in the public docs? Also: how does this interact with OpenAI-compatibility layer tool-calling? Could constraints be passed through the compat adapter unchanged?
Maya Patel: Added docs snippet and ensured the OpenAI compat adapter forwards the constraint payload as-is, plus a translation layer for regex flags. Documented behavior in the adapter docstring.
Sofia Martinez: Found a flaky test in streaming_integration on macOS (emoji handling). I updated the fuzz seed and ran CI twice — second run passed.
Maya Patel: Flaky test addressed by normalizing grapheme boundaries in the test harness; added retry for known flakiness.
Riley Chen: Approved after the small nits were fixed.
testing_notes: Unit tests: added 36 new unit tests covering tokenizer/regex/CFG intersections. Integration: 4 new streaming e2e tests with function-calling + structured-output. Fuzz: added corpus of 1200 examples including multi-codepoint emoji, combined diacritics, and RTL characters.
release_notes: Fix: structured output constrained decoding now correctly handles tokenizer boundary edgecases and Unicode grapheme clusters for CFG and regex backends; more deterministic errors for malformed constraints.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: subtle behavior change for malformed regex/CFG; Mitigation: return structured error metadata and feature-flag the strict normalization for a rolling canary on Dedicated clusters.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag 'constrained_strict_normalization' via console for staged rollout. Monitor metrics: constrained.decode.errors and structured_output.invalid_json-rate.
